---
title: "Glen Canyon Dam"
---

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
devtools::load_all()
library(tidyverse)
```

Two daily discharge series on the Colorado River, from USGS NWIS (`dataRetrieval::readNWISdv`, parameter `00060`, 1950–2025):

- `cisco_cfs`: Colorado River near Cisco, UT (site `09180500`) — ~280 river miles upstream of Glen Canyon Dam, above Lake Powell. Flow here is essentially natural: snowmelt-driven, with a strong spring pulse and low winter baseflow.
- `leesferry_cfs`: Colorado River at Lees Ferry, AZ (site `09380000`) — immediately downstream of Glen Canyon Dam, the standard compliance point for Colorado River Compact accounting.

Glen Canyon Dam closed on **1963-03-13**, and Lake Powell filled gradually until reaching first full pool in **1980**. Before closure, Lees Ferry flow is essentially a translated, lightly attenuated copy of Cisco flow (plus minor ungauged tributary inflow over the intervening reach) — the two should be strongly correlated. After closure, Lake Powell decouples the two: releases at Lees Ferry are set by hydropower demand and Bureau of Reclamation operating rules (historically a smoothed, sometimes sub-daily "hydropeaking" pattern), not by the timing of upstream inflow. The correlation between the series is expected to drop sharply at the closure date, with a possible further shift as the reservoir's buffering capacity grew through 1980. This gives a real change point with a known date and mechanism, rather than one inferred after the fact — the case this project's tests want most.

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| label: gcd-load

cisco <- read_csv("../data/real-data/glen-canyon-dam/cisco-daily.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(Date = as.Date(Date))

leesferry <- read_csv("../data/real-data/glen-canyon-dam/leesferry-daily.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(Date = as.Date(Date))

X <- inner_join(cisco, leesferry, by = "Date") |>
  arrange(Date)

dam_closure <- as.Date("1963-03-13")
full_pool   <- as.Date("1980-06-30")
```

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-gcd-raw
#| fig-cap: "Daily discharge, Colorado River near Cisco, UT vs. at Lees Ferry, AZ. Vertical line marks Glen Canyon Dam closure (1963-03-13)."

X |>
  select(Date, cisco_cfs, leesferry_cfs) |>
  pivot_longer(-Date, names_to = "series", values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(Date, value, color = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = dam_closure, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Cisco (upstream) vs. Lees Ferry (downstream of Glen Canyon Dam)",
       x = NULL, y = "Discharge (cfs)", color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Daily discharge is heavily autocorrelated (multi-day travel time, multi-week snowmelt recession) and the raw series span 5+ orders of magnitude of hydropeaking noise post-dam, so we aggregate to monthly means before any ECE diagnostics, mirroring `elnino.qmd`.

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| label: gcd-monthly

X_monthly <- X |>
  mutate(year = year(Date), month = month(Date)) |>
  group_by(year, month) |>
  summarize(cisco_cfs = mean(cisco_cfs), leesferry_cfs = mean(leesferry_cfs), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(sprintf("%d-%02d-01", year, month))) |>
  arrange(date)

X_mat <- as.matrix(X_monthly[, c("cisco_cfs", "leesferry_cfs")])
```

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-gcd-monthly
#| fig-cap: "Monthly mean discharge. Vertical line marks Glen Canyon Dam closure."

X_monthly |>
  select(date, cisco_cfs, leesferry_cfs) |>
  pivot_longer(-date, names_to = "series", values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(date, value, color = series)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = dam_closure, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Monthly Mean Discharge", x = NULL, y = "Discharge (cfs)", color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| label: gcd-rolling

win <- 25 # matches elnino.qmd / mental-load.qmd
roll_mat <- apply(X_mat, 2, function(col) rolling_mean(col, win))
colnames(roll_mat) <- colnames(X_mat)
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Plot

```{R plot-gcd}
#| echo: false

par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(0, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(4, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))

for (i in 1:2) {
  plot(X_mat[, i], type = "l", xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n",
        ylab = colnames(X_mat)[i], cex.lab = 0.8)
  axis(2, labels = FALSE, tck = -0.02)
  lines(roll_mat[, i], col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
}
axis(1)
mtext("Month index (1950–2025)", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 2.5)
```

## ACF

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Naive

```{R acf-gcd-naive}
#| echo: false

par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(2, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))

for (i in 1:2) {
  resid_i <- na.omit(X_mat[, i] - roll_mat[, i])
  acf(resid_i, main = "", xlab = "", ylab = colnames(X_mat)[i])
}
mtext("Lag (months)", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 0.5)
```


## Downsampling

Keep every 3rd observation (`k = 3`), matching `elnino.qmd`.

```{R downsample-gcd}
#| echo: false

k_ds <- 3
idx  <- seq(1, nrow(X_mat), by = k_ds)
X_ds <- X_mat[idx, ]

win_ds <- 25 # same fixed window as the full-sample case
roll_mat_ds <- apply(X_ds, 2, function(col) rolling_mean(col, win_ds))
colnames(roll_mat_ds) <- colnames(X_ds)
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Plot

```{R plot-gcd-downsampled}
#| echo: false

par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(0, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(4, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))

for (i in 1:2) {
  plot(X_ds[, i], type = "l", xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n",
        ylab = colnames(X_ds)[i], cex.lab = 0.8)
  axis(2, labels = FALSE, tck = -0.02)
  lines(roll_mat_ds[, i], col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
}
axis(1)
mtext("Index (every 3rd month)", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 2.5)
```

## Pre/Post-Dam Correlation

A direct check of the mechanistic story: raw Pearson correlation of monthly means, split at dam closure.

```{R gcd-split-cor}
#| echo: false

pre  <- X_monthly |> filter(date < dam_closure)
post_filling <- X_monthly |> filter(date >= dam_closure, date < full_pool)
post <- X_monthly |> filter(date >= full_pool)

tibble(
  period = c("Pre-dam (< 1963-03)", "Filling Lake Powell (1963-03 to 1980-06)", "Post-full-pool (>= 1980-06)"),
  n_months = c(nrow(pre), nrow(post_filling), nrow(post)),
  cor = c(cor(pre$cisco_cfs, pre$leesferry_cfs),
          cor(post_filling$cisco_cfs, post_filling$leesferry_cfs),
          cor(post$cisco_cfs, post$leesferry_cfs))
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```
